description.summary: server-side material effects behind and around a surface

protocol.description:
This protocol lets a client ask the compositor to render material effects for one of its surfaces: a blurred, tinted and saturated backdrop behind a region of it, a refractive rim along that region's edge, a corner radius clipping the surface itself, and a drop shadow cast underneath it.
The point of doing this server-side is that a client cannot do it at all. What sits behind a surface belongs to other clients, and a translucent surface never gets to see it. The compositor does, and it already has the composited frame in a texture when it draws the surface.
Shapes are parametric rather than pixel regions. A wl_region is a set of integer rectangles, which cannot describe a rounded corner without thousands of one-pixel steps; the shapes here are fed to a signed distance field in the compositor's fragment shader, so they are antialiased at the output's real resolution with no per-rectangle cost.
Warning! The protocol described in this file is currently in the testing phase. Backward compatible changes may be added together with the corresponding interface version bump. Backward incompatible changes can only be done by creating a new major version of the extension.

interface.name: crownos_shape_manager_v1
interface.description:
A global factory for crownos_shape_v1 objects.
Shapes are not bound to a surface and carry no effect of their own. They are plain geometry, created here and then passed to the requests of crownos_background_effect_surface_v1 that take one.

request.name: destroy
request.description:
Destroy the shape factory.
Shapes created through this manager are unaffected and stay valid until they are destroyed individually.

request.name: create_shape
request.description:
Create a new shape object with no primitives in it.
A shape with no primitives covers nothing. Passing one to an effect is not an error; it simply leaves that effect covering no pixels, which is how an effect is turned off without destroying the object that carries it.

interface.name: crownos_shape_v1
interface.description:
A shape is the union of the primitives added to it. Primitives may overlap; the union is what the compositor renders, and overlapping interiors are not double-counted.
All coordinates and lengths are in surface-local coordinates, the same space wl_surface.set_input_region and xdg_surface.set_window_geometry use. They are therefore independent of the buffer scale and of any viewport transform the surface carries.
A shape is copied when it is used. The requests that take a shape read its primitives at the time of the request, so the client may destroy the shape, or keep adding to it for a different effect, as soon as the request has been issued. Changing a shape never retroactively changes an effect that was set from it.
The compositor may limit how many primitives it renders for one shape. A shape past that limit is not an error; the surplus primitives are simply not drawn, because a client that asks for a thousand of them wants a picture, not a material.

entry.name: invalid_size
entry.summary: a primitive was given a negative width or height

request.name: destroy
request.description:
Destroy the shape object.
Effects already set from this shape keep the geometry they copied.

request.name: add_rounded_rect

description.summary: add a rounded rectangle to the shape

request.description:
Add an axis-aligned rectangle with uniformly rounded corners.
The radius is clamped to half the shorter side, so a radius larger than the rectangle produces a stadium, never an inverted shape. A radius of zero is a sharp rectangle.
Passing a negative width or height raises an invalid_size error. Zero width or height is allowed and contributes nothing.

request.name: add_circle

description.summary: add a circle to the shape

request.description: Add a circle. A radius of zero contributes nothing.

interface.name: crownos_background_effect_manager_v1
interface.description: A global factory for crownos_background_effect_surface_v1 objects, and the object that tells a client which effects this compositor will actually render.

entry.name: effect_exists
entry.summary: the surface already has a background effect object

enum.name: capability

description.summary: effects the compositor is willing to render

enum.description: Which of the requests below do something. A compositor may withhold a capability because the user turned the effect off, because the renderer could not compile the shaders, or because it is running on battery.

request.name: destroy
request.description: Destroy the factory. Effect objects created through it are unaffected.

request.name: get_effect_surface

description.summary: get an effect object for a surface

request.description:
Create an object through which background effects are set on the given surface.
A surface may have at most one such object alive at a time. Asking for a second one while the first is alive raises an effect_exists error. The surface is free to get a new one once the previous object has been destroyed.

event.name: capabilities
event.description:
Sent when the manager is bound, and again every time the set changes.
When a capability goes away the corresponding effect stops being rendered even if it was set before, and a client that depends on it — a panel relying on blur for its text to be legible — should paint its own background instead. State set for a withdrawn capability is remembered, not discarded, and takes effect again if it returns.

interface.name: crownos_background_effect_surface_v1

description.summary: manage background effects for a surface

interface.description:
Sets the material effects rendered for one wl_surface.
All requests on this interface are double-buffered in the surface's pending state, in the sense of wl_surface.commit. They take effect at the next commit of the associated surface, so a client resizing its window and changing its effects in the same commit never shows one without the other.
Effects are clipped to the surface for the purposes of input and window geometry: the shadow drawn outside the surface is decoration, it is never part of the input region and never enlarges the window's geometry.
If the wl_surface is destroyed first, this object becomes inert. Every subsequent request other than destroy raises a surface_destroyed error.

entry.name: surface_destroyed
entry.summary: the wl_surface was destroyed before this object

entry.name: invalid_saturation
entry.summary: a negative saturation multiplier was given

request.name: destroy

description.summary: remove the effects from the surface

request.description:
Destroy the object.
The effects are removed on the next commit of the associated surface, like any other double-buffered change, rather than at the moment this request arrives. A client that wants them gone immediately destroys this object and commits.

request.name: set_corner_radius
request.description:
Clip the surface, and every effect set on it, to a rounded rectangle covering the whole surface with this corner radius, in surface-local pixels.
The radius is clamped to half the shorter side of the surface. A radius of zero, the initial value, leaves the surface square.

request.name: set_border

description.summary: draw a refractive rim along the effect's edge

request.description:
Draw a rim of the given width, in surface-local pixels, just inside the edge of the blur shape — or of the whole surface if no blur shape was set.
The rim is not a stroke of a colour the client picks. It is the compositor's rendering of light passing through the edge of the material: the backdrop is refracted through it and comes back more saturated than the blur behind it, which is what makes the edge read as a bevel rather than as a painted line.
A width of zero, the initial value, draws no rim.

request.name: set_blur

description.summary: blur the backdrop under a shape

request.description:
Blur what the compositor composites behind the surface, within the given shape, and tint and saturate the result.
A null shape means the whole surface, clipped by the corner radius. A non-null shape is copied by this request and clipped to the surface.
blur_radius is in surface-local pixels and is a request, not a promise: the compositor maps it onto whatever its blur pipeline can express. A blur_radius of zero, the initial value, turns the blur off, and with it the rim, the tint and the saturation, which have nothing to sit on.
tint_color is ARGB8888, not premultiplied, in the surface's colour space. Its alpha is how much of it is mixed over the blurred backdrop: fully transparent leaves the backdrop's own colours.
saturation multiplies the blurred backdrop's chroma about its luma before the tint is applied. 1.0 leaves it alone, values above 1.0 are the vibrancy that makes a colour show through frosted glass, 0.0 is greyscale. A negative value raises an invalid_saturation error.

arg.name: shape
arg.summary: the shape to blur; null means the entire surface

arg.name: tint_color
arg.summary: ARGB8888 tint mixed over the blur

request.name: set_shadow

description.summary: cast a drop shadow under a shape

request.description:
Draw a blurred, offset silhouette of the given shape underneath the surface.
A null shape means the whole surface, clipped by the corner radius. A non-null shape is copied by this request.
The shadow is drawn outside the surface and is therefore not clipped to it. It is decoration only: it does not extend the input region, the window geometry, or the area the surface is considered to occupy for layout.
shadow_radius is the blur radius of the silhouette in surface-local pixels; zero, the initial value, draws no shadow. offset_x and offset_y displace it in surface-local pixels, positive being right and down.
color is ARGB8888, not premultiplied. Its alpha is the shadow's opacity at the centre of the silhouette.

arg.name: shape
arg.summary: the shape to cast; null means the entire surface
